review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

5:1.sourceText: Πᾶς γὰρ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐξ ἀνθρώπων λαμβανόμενος ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων καθίσταται τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, ἵνα προσφέρῃ δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίας ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν,
5:1.targetText: For every chief priest taken out of men is set in things [pertaining] to God in behalf of men, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,

groups.note: The actual nominalized τὰ πρός expression gives the things pertaining to God as the accusative respect/complement of the priestly appointment. English in things pertaining to expresses that full relation, including bracketed pertaining, without a separately written Greek in or pertain word.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:2.sourceText: μετριοπαθεῖν δυνάμενος τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσιν καὶ πλανωμένοις, ἐπεὶ καὶ αὐτὸς περίκειται ἀσθένειαν,
5:2.targetText: being able to be gentle to those being ignorant and going astray, since he is also surrounded with weakness;

groups.note: The actual μετριοπαθεῖν means deal moderately/gently with people, showing measured forbearance; LSV to be gentle retains that real verbal head, not a different Greek gentle adjective.
The actual being-surrounded predicate περίκειται takes weakness as its encircling condition; LSV is surrounded with expresses that one predicate without a new Greek passive verb.

5:3.sourceText: καὶ δι’ αὐτὴν ὀφείλει, καθὼς περὶ τοῦ λαοῦ, οὕτως καὶ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ προσφέρειν περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν.
5:3.targetText: and because of this [weakness] he ought, just as for the people, so also for himself, to bring forward [sacrifices] for sins;

groups.note: The actual feminine pronoun αὐτήν refers to the preceding weakness; LSV renders this and supplies the antecedent noun separately in brackets. The pronoun is not relabeled as the Greek weakness noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats the antecedent noun weakness to clarify this; N1904 has only the anaphoric pronoun at this occurrence. The actual weakness noun remains at5:2, not a new noun written in5:3.
English supplies the sacrifice object of bring forward from the priestly context; no sacrifice noun is written at this infinitive.

5:4.sourceText: καὶ οὐχ ἑαυτῷ τις λαμβάνει τὴν τιμήν, ἀλλὰ καλούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καθώσπερ καὶ Ἀαρών.
5:4.targetText: and no one takes the honor to himself, but he who is called by God, as also Aaron.

groups.note: The actual not plus indefinite anyone, οὐχ ... τις, jointly yields no one; neither source component is dropped.

The actual passive called participle identifies the called person in contrast to self-appointment; LSV expands that real personal predicate as he who is called without separately written source he/who/is words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:5.sourceText: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐχ ἑαυτὸν ἐδόξασεν γενηθῆναι ἀρχιερέα, ἀλλ’ ὁ λαλήσας πρὸς αὐτόν Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε·
5:5.targetText: So also the Christ did not glorify Himself to become Chief Priest, but He who spoke to Him: “You are My Son, today I have begotten You”;

5:6.sourceText: καθὼς καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.
5:6.targetText: just as He also says in another [place], “You [are] a priest throughout the age, according to the order of Melchizedek”;

groups.note: The actual substantival other demonstrative identifies another cited passage; English bracketed place states that contextual nominal head without a separate Greek place noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

5:7.sourceText: ὃς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ δεήσεις τε καὶ ἱκετηρίας πρὸς τὸν δυνάμενον σῴζειν αὐτὸν ἐκ θανάτου μετὰ κραυγῆς ἰσχυρᾶς καὶ δακρύων προσενέγκας καὶ εἰσακουσθεὶς ἀπὸ τῆς εὐλαβείας,
5:7.targetText: who in the days of His flesh having offered up both prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears to Him who was able to save Him from death, and having been heard in respect to that which He feared,

groups.note: The actual present being-able participle is placed in the past days-of-flesh narrative; LSV was able supplies that English temporal form with the genuine ability predicate, not an independent Greek was verb.

Greek ἀπό relates the hearing to the fear/reverence phrase. It has been understood causally, because of reverence, or as release from fear; LSV in respect to keeps an interpretive relation without a separate source respect noun.

The actual article plus εὐλάβεια noun denotes caution/reverence or fear/anxiety. LSV recasts the noun as the object-relative expression that which He feared. This retains the uniquely identifiable fear/reverence head with its state-to-object wording difference explicit; it is not a Greek φοβέομαι verb or an independently written which/He pronoun. Thayer2124 discusses both reverence and anxiety interpretations at this verse.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:8.sourceText: καίπερ ὢν Υἱός, ἔμαθεν ἀφ’ ὧν ἔπαθεν τὴν ὑπακοήν,
5:8.targetText: though being a Son, [He] learned obedience by the things which He suffered,

groups.note: The actual finite third-person learned verb encodes its subject; English bracketed He states that same subject without a second original pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:9.sourceText: καὶ τελειωθεὶς ἐγένετο πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ αἴτιος σωτηρίας αἰωνίου,
5:9.targetText: and having been made perfect, He became the cause of continuous salvation to all those obeying Him,

groups.note: The actual causal/responsible adjective αἴτιος is predicated of the saving person and rendered the cause; the exact head remains an adjective, not a substituted αἰτία noun.

5:10.sourceText: προσαγορευθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀρχιερεὺς κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.
5:10.targetText: having been called by God a Chief Priest according to the order of Melchizedek,

groups.note: The actual προσαγορεύω passive denotes formal naming/designation as Chief Priest; LSV having been called retains this head, not a substituted ordinary καλέω verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:11.sourceText: Περὶ οὗ πολὺς ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος καὶ δυσερμήνευτος λέγειν, ἐπεὶ νωθροὶ γεγόνατε ταῖς ἀκοαῖς.
5:11.targetText: concerning the Word, of whom we have much [to speak], and of hard explanation to say, since you have become dull of hearing,

groups.note: The actual dative us participates in the nominal our-discourse-is-much expression; LSV recasts that possession as we have. No original ἔχω having verb is printed here.

In N1904 περὶ οὗ πολὺς ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος, λόγος is the discourse/account that is much and difficult to state about the preceding priestly subject. Displayed LSV fronts and capitalizes Word as a topic in concerning the Word, of whom. The actual lexical head is retained with this altered clause-role interpretation explicit; the original does not thereby assert a divine Logos title. The added to speak is separately explained, while the actual saying infinitive retains to say.
The actual hard-to-interpret/explain adjective δυσερμήνευτος qualifies the discourse; LSV expresses that quality as of hard explanation without an independent Greek explanation noun.

The actual dative plural hearing/faculties phrase gives the respect of dullness; English of hearing renders the whole case relation with a singular abstract noun, not an independent Greek of preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a to-speak complement after we have much when recasting the Greek our-discourse-is-much phrase; it is not a second occurrence of the later written λέγειν, to say, and the fronted English Word is a different clause role from this talking-about-it addition.

5:12.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον, πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκειν ὑμᾶς τινα τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος, οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς.
5:12.targetText: for even owing to be teachers, because of the time, again you have need that one teach you what [are] the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have become having need of milk, and not of strong food,

groups.note: The nominalizing article introduces the teaching infinitive as the content of need; LSV recasts that complement as a finite that-clause, not an independent original ὅτι connector.
The actual indefinite accusative τινα is someone as the teaching subject, rendered one. It is not the English what question frame or the following elements article.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an indirect-question/copula frame what are before the elements; N1904 directly names the elements as the teaching object, without an interrogative or finite be verb there.
English coordinates the contrasting milk/not-solid-food objects with an added and; N1904 directly negates the solid-food phrase without a second conjunction.

5:13.sourceText: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος ἄπειρος λόγου δικαιοσύνης, νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν·
5:13.targetText: for everyone who is partaking of milk [is] unskilled in the word of righteousness—for he is an infant,

groups.note: The actual genitive word phrase gives the area in which the milk-partaker is inexperienced; LSV expresses that relation as in the word, without an independently printed Greek in preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

5:14.sourceText: τελείων δέ ἐστιν ἡ στερεὰ τροφή, τῶν διὰ τὴν ἕξιν τὰ αἰσθητήρια γεγυμνασμένα ἐχόντων πρὸς διάκρισιν καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ.
5:14.targetText: and the strong food is of perfect men, who because of the use are having the senses exercised, to both the discernment of good and of evil.

groups.note: The actual genitive plural perfect/mature adjective is substantival for mature people; LSV perfect men makes that human head explicit without a separately written Greek men noun.
The actual habit/practice noun ἕξις denotes trained use or exercise; LSV use retains that head, not a different Greek utility noun.
